tickets.title: Replace Next.js 14 with a Vite React 19 TS scaffold
tickets.summary: The frontend builds as a static Vite + React 19 + TypeScript SPA and Next.js is gone.
tickets.description: Implements overview 4.4 ("Vite + React 19 + TypeScript single-page app, static files in a GCS bucket ... Replaces Next.js 14 (G-13, G-57)") and ADR-019. In frontend/: add vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, react/react-dom 19, typescript; index.html + src/main.tsx entry; vite.config.ts (dev server proxies /v1 to the compose gateway so the SPA stays same-origin); keep tailwind, zustand, react-markdown, eventsource-parser only if later tickets use them. Move existing components/hooks from src/app + src/components into a Vite layout without behaviour changes (still the MVP header-user flow until E8-T3). Update the E0-T10 artefacts for Vite: `npm run test` (vitest, jsdom), `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), and the frontend dev Dockerfile (vite dev server, port documented). Remove next, eslint-config-next, next.config.mjs, next-env.d.ts; replace with plain eslint config. Pin Vite and TypeScript versions in package.json (stack.md: pin at implementation). Out of scope: bucket/ALB deploy (E10), auth, new features. Use SPA fallback so /t/<slug> deep links work in the dev server and `vite preview`.
acceptance_criteria: Given a clean checkout, when `npm ci && npm run build` runs in frontend/, then it exits 0 and dist/index.html plus hashed assets exist.
Given package.json, when searched, then no `next` or `eslint-config-next` dependency and no next.config.mjs remain (checked by a vitest/grep test or CI step).
Given the dev server or `vite preview`, when GET /t/acme is requested, then index.html is returned (SPA fallback), asserted by a vitest or curl check.
`npm run typecheck` and `npm run test` exit 0, with at least one smoke test rendering <App/>.
The frontend dev Dockerfile builds (`docker build`) and serves the Vite dev server.

tickets.title: Add tenant discovery at /t/<slug>
tickets.summary: The SPA resolves the firm from the URL slug through the public tenant endpoint and shows a not-found state.
tickets.description: Implements overview 8.2 step 1 and 6.1 `GET /v1/tenants/{slug}` -> `{display_name, idp_tenant_id}` only; 404 `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`. Add react-router route `/t/:slug`; typed `fetchTenant(slug)` in src/lib/api.ts (unauthenticated, no Authorization header); a tenant context holding {slug, display_name, idp_tenant_id}; the firm display_name shown in the header. Unknown slug renders a firm-not-found page keyed by the error code (no crash). Routes outside /t/:slug show a short 'use your firm link' page. Out of scope: sign-in (E8-T3), the endpoint itself (E1-T16).
acceptance_criteria: Given a mocked 200 `{display_name:'Acme', idp_tenant_id:'t-1'}`, when /t/acme renders, then 'Acme' appears and the tenant context holds idp_tenant_id 't-1' (vitest + testing-library).
Given a mocked 404 `TENANT_NOT_FOUND`, when /t/nope renders, then the not-found page shows and no sign-in form renders.
Given the request is captured, when fetchTenant runs, then it carries no Authorization header (unit test).
Given a network failure, when /t/acme renders, then a retryable error state shows, not an unhandled exception.

tickets.title: Add Identity Platform tenant sign-in with in-memory token
tickets.summary: An advisor signs in to their firm's IdP tenant and API calls carry the ID token, never persisted to localStorage.
tickets.description: Implements overview 8.2 steps 2-3 and ADR-010. Use the Firebase/Identity Platform web SDK: set `auth.tenantId = idp_tenant_id` from E8-T2, email/password sign-in, token from `getIdToken()` kept only in memory (SDK auth persistence set to `inMemoryPersistence`; no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB or cookie for the token). Build an `apiFetch` wrapper that adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and refreshes via getIdToken. After sign-in call `GET /v1/me` and store {advisor_id, display_name, role, tier}. Provide sign-out. Remove the MVP UserSwitcher/X-User header flow. Config: Firebase web config via Vite env (VITE_*), no secrets. Out of scope: SSO, tenant onboarding (E1/E10), 401 UI handling (E8-T4).
acceptance_criteria: Given a signed-in session in a vitest test with a mocked SDK, when apiFetch is called, then the request has `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Given sign-in completes, when localStorage, sessionStorage and document.cookie are inspected, then none contains the token string (unit test; repeated in Playwright E8-T11).
Given the SDK auth instance, when initialised, then tenantId equals the discovered idp_tenant_id and persistence is in-memory (unit test).
Given sign-out, when called, then the in-memory token and /v1/me state are cleared and the sign-in form shows.
grep of src/ finds no `X-User` header or UserSwitcher.

tickets.title: Map API error codes to UI states with 401 and 429 handling
tickets.summary: Every API error renders a fixed, code-keyed message and 401 and 429 never crash the app.
tickets.description: Implements overview 4.4 'error states keyed by error code' and 6.1 error shape `{"error":{code,message,request_id,retryable}}`. Add src/lib/errors.ts: parse the error body into ApiError; a table keyed by every 6.1 code (UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, INPUT_TOO_LONG, INPUT_BLOCKED, GUARD_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, TENANT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED, NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION, LLM_UNAVAILABLE, RETRIEVAL_UNAVAILABLE, TURN_INTERRUPTED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, INTERNAL) to client-owned copy and a retry hint; unknown codes fall back to INTERNAL copy. Never display server `message` text verbatim as HTML; show request_id for support. 401: refresh token once, retry once, else return to sign-in. 429: read `Retry-After`, show a countdown and disable send until it elapses. Add an error boundary. Out of scope: SSE-specific handling (E8-T5/T6).
acceptance_criteria: Given each code in the 6.1 list, when mapped, then a non-empty message exists (table-driven vitest over all codes) and an unknown code maps to the INTERNAL copy.
Given a 429 with `Retry-After: 5`, when the chat send is attempted, then the send button is disabled and a countdown shows, re-enabling after 5 s (fake timers).
Given a 401 whose retry after token refresh also returns 401, when it occurs, then the sign-in view shows and no uncaught exception is logged.
Given a render error in a child, when thrown, then the error boundary shows a fallback (unit test).

tickets.title: Build fetch-based SSE client with resume and idempotency
tickets.summary: A typed SSE client posts a chat turn with an Idempotency-Key and resumes from Last-Event-ID after a drop.
tickets.description: Implements overview 6.2 and 6.1. src/lib/sse.ts, fetch + ReadableStream (not EventSource, because of the Authorization header and POST), parsing with eventsource-parser. Typed discriminated union for events turn, meta, tool, delta, citation, refusal, error, done with the 6.2 data shapes. `sendTurn({conversation_id?, message})`: generate `Idempotency-Key` (crypto.randomUUID) per user submit, POST /v1/chat, record `turn_id` from the `turn` event and the last `id:` seq. On a transport drop before `done`/`error`, reconnect to `GET /v1/chat/{turn_id}/events` with `Last-Event-ID: <last seq>`, bounded retries with backoff (config constants), ignoring events with seq <= last seen (no duplicate deltas). If the drop happens before the `turn` event, retry POST with the same key. `error` event with TURN_INTERRUPTED retryable: surface to caller, which resubmits with a NEW key. 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED surfaces as an ApiError. Support AbortController. Ignore heartbeat comment lines. Out of scope: server side (E4).
acceptance_criteria: Given a stream cut after seq 3, when the client reconnects, then the GET carries `Last-Event-ID: 3` and the output has no duplicated delta text (vitest with a fake fetch).
Given a drop before the `turn` event, when retried, then the POST reuses the same Idempotency-Key.
Given an `error {TURN_INTERRUPTED, retryable:true}`, when received, then the client emits it to the caller and does not auto-resume; a resubmit uses a different key (unit test).
Given a heartbeat comment line and a replayed event with seq <= last seen, when parsed, then neither reaches the caller.
Given an unknown event name, when received, then it is ignored without throwing.

tickets.title: Render the streamed turn with meta notice and refusal
tickets.summary: The chat view shows deltas as they arrive, tool status, a degraded-retrieval notice, refusals and errors.
tickets.description: Implements overview 6.2 behaviour in the UI. Rewrite useChat (zustand store) on top of E8-T5: `turn` sets ids; `delta` appends to the in-progress assistant message; `tool` shows a status chip (tool name and status only); `meta` with retrieval_degraded=true shows a visible notice ('answer built with reduced ranking quality', reason optional), stored on the message; `refusal` NO_FIRM_DOCUMENTATION shows the refusal message and, if escalate_offer, an escalation hint (no endpoint call beyond arch); `error` shows the code-keyed state from E8-T4 with Retry when retryable; `done` finalises with message_id and finish_reason (max_tokens shows a 'truncated' note). Disable input while streaming; Stop button aborts. Remove client-side citation parsing of `[n]` (server emits citations; E8-T7). Out of scope: markdown (E8-T7), history (E8-T8).
acceptance_criteria: Given a scripted event sequence turn, delta x3, done, when processed, then the message text equals the concatenated deltas and finish state is set (vitest store test).
Given `meta {retrieval_degraded:true}`, when received, then the degraded notice is in the DOM; given false, it is absent.
Given `refusal {escalate_offer:true}`, when received, then the refusal view and escalation hint render and no assistant text is shown.
Given `error {code:'LLM_UNAVAILABLE',retryable:true}`, when received, then the mapped message and a Retry button show; given retryable false, no Retry button.
Given the Stop button, when clicked mid-stream, then the fetch is aborted and input is re-enabled.

tickets.title: Render sanitized markdown, citations with excerpts and stale badges
tickets.summary: Answers render as sanitized markdown with server-emitted citations, excerpts and stale badges.
tickets.description: Implements overview 4.4 'citations with excerpts, stale badges ... Renders sanitized markdown only' and the `citation` event `{index, chunk_id, source_title, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, stale, excerpt}`. Markdown via react-markdown with no raw HTML (no rehype-raw), plus an explicit sanitiser (rehype-sanitize with a minimal allowlist; links limited to http/https/mailto and rel=noopener noreferrer; images not rendered). Inline `[n]` markers link to the citation with that index from `citation` events only; a marker with no matching event renders as plain text. Citation panel lists source_title, regulatory_ref, last_reviewed_at, excerpt (as text, never HTML) and a StaleBadge when stale=true. Reuse/adapt existing MarkdownContent, CitationPanel, StaleBadge, SourcesPanel. Also used for history messages (E8-T8). Out of scope: client-side citation verification.
acceptance_criteria: Given answer text containing ``, `` and `[x](javascript:alert(1))`, when rendered, then the DOM has no script/img element, no onerror attribute and no javascript: href (vitest + testing-library).
Given a `citation` event with stale=true, when rendered, then the stale badge shows; with stale=false it does not.
Given a citation excerpt `x`, when rendered, then it appears as literal text with no element.
Given `[2]` in the text with no citation index 2, when rendered, then it is plain text, not a link.
Given a citation with index 1, when `[1]` is clicked, then the panel entry for index 1 is highlighted.

tickets.title: Add conversation history list, load and delete
tickets.summary: An advisor can list, reopen and delete their own conversations.
tickets.description: Implements overview 6.1: `GET /v1/conversations?cursor`, `GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages?cursor` (messages with citations, redacted), `DELETE /v1/conversations/{id}` (204). Sidebar list with cursor 'load more'; selecting loads messages (rendered with E8-T7 including citations and stale badges, and the stored retrieval_degraded notice if the response includes it; if the response shape lacks it, see questions); new chat button; delete with confirm, removes from list and clears view if active. Subsequent sends in an opened conversation pass its `conversation_id`. Empty and error states use E8-T4. Out of scope: search, rename, escalations list.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mocked first page with next cursor, when 'load more' is clicked, then the request carries `?cursor=<value>` and rows append (vitest).
Given a conversation is selected, when messages load, then citations render under the assistant message.
Given delete is confirmed and the API returns 204, when processed, then the row disappears; given it returns 403, then the row stays and the code-keyed error shows.
Given an opened conversation, when a message is sent, then the POST body contains that conversation_id.

tickets.title: Add thumbs feedback on assistant messages
tickets.summary: An advisor can rate an answer up or down with an optional comment.
tickets.description: Implements overview 6.1 `POST /v1/messages/{id}/feedback` body `{score: -1 | 1, comment?: string}` -> 204. Thumbs up/down on each completed assistant message (message_id from `done` or history); thumbs down opens an optional comment field. State: pending, saved, failed (retry); selection persists in view after reload of history only if the messages API returns it (otherwise questions). Disabled while streaming and for refusal/error messages. Out of scope: eval pipeline (backend).
acceptance_criteria: Given thumbs-up on message m1, when clicked, then POST /v1/messages/m1/feedback is sent with body `{score:1}` (vitest fake fetch).
Given thumbs-down with comment 'wrong', when submitted, then the body is `{score:-1, comment:'wrong'}`.
Given a 500/INTERNAL response, when received, then the button shows failed with Retry and no exception escapes.
Given a message still streaming, when rendered, then feedback buttons are disabled.

tickets.title: Set up Playwright and an auditable test harness for the SPA
tickets.summary: Playwright runs against the built SPA with a controllable API and IdP stub, wired into CI.
tickets.description: Implements overview 4.4 'Tests: vitest + Playwright'. Add @playwright/test (pinned), playwright.config.ts that serves `vite preview` of the production build, a fixture API stub (route-level mocking via page.route, plus a small SSE stub server able to emit scripted events with ids, drop the connection at a given seq and honour Last-Event-ID) and an Identity Platform auth stub or the Firebase Auth emulator (decision in questions; default the emulator with two tenants `acme` and `globex`). Add npm script `test:e2e` and a CI job step. One smoke spec: /t/acme loads and shows the firm name. Out of scope: the scenario specs (E8-T11, E8-T12) and running against the real deployed stack.
acceptance_criteria: Given `npm run test:e2e`, when run in CI, then the smoke spec passes and the HTML report is uploaded as an artifact.
Given the SSE stub scripted to drop after seq 2, when a client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID: 2`, then the stub replays from seq 3 (stub self-test).
Given tenants acme and globex are seeded, when /t/acme and /t/globex load, then each shows its own display_name.
Given the workflow file, when parsed, then the e2e job runs after the build step (CI config check).

tickets.title: Add Playwright specs for sign-in, streamed cited answer and feedback
tickets.summary: E2E proves two-tenant sign-in, a streamed cited answer, a stale badge and thumbs feedback.
tickets.description: Part of E8 Done-when. Specs: (1) sign in as advisor of acme and as advisor of globex; each sees its own firm name and `/v1/me` display_name; a tenant-mismatched token attempt shows the UNAUTHENTICATED state. (2) ask a question: deltas stream into the answer incrementally (assert partial text before `done`), `meta` degraded notice appears when scripted, citations with excerpts render, one stale=true citation shows the stale badge. (3) thumbs-up and thumbs-down send the correct feedback request. (4) conversation history shows the turn after reload. Out of scope: failure scenarios (E8-T12).
acceptance_criteria: Given two seeded tenants, when each signs in, then each page shows its own firm name and no cross-tenant data (Playwright assertion).
Given a scripted stream of 3 deltas then done, when asked, then the answer text is observed with partial content before the final delta.
Given a citation scripted with stale=true, when rendered, then `getByText` for the stale badge is visible; a stale=false citation has none.
Given thumbs-up click, when sent, then page.waitForRequest sees POST /v1/messages/<id>/feedback with `{score:1}`.

tickets.title: Add Playwright specs for resume, 429, 401 and XSS safety
tickets.summary: E2E proves resume after disconnect, graceful 429 and 401, no unsanitized HTML and no token in localStorage.
tickets.description: Part of E8 Done-when. Specs: (1) mid-stream disconnect at seq N: the stub drops the connection; the UI reconnects with `Last-Event-ID: N`, final text equals the full answer with no duplicated text. (2) 429 with Retry-After on POST /v1/chat: the rate-limit message and countdown show, the page remains usable, send re-enables. (3) 401 on an API call: token refresh retried once, then the sign-in view shows, no page error (`page.on('pageerror')` count 0). (4) Injected payload: the answer text and a citation excerpt contain `` and ``; after render `window.__xss` is undefined and no such elements exist. (5) After sign-in and a chat, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB dumps do not contain the ID token string. Also covers TURN_INTERRUPTED: Retry resubmits with a new Idempotency-Key.
acceptance_criteria: Given a drop after seq 2 of 5 events, when the test completes, then the request log shows a GET with `Last-Event-ID: 2` and the answer contains each delta exactly once.
Given a 429 `Retry-After: 2`, when sent, then the countdown is visible, `pageerror` count is 0 and send is enabled after about 2 s.
Given 401 twice, when it occurs, then the sign-in view is visible and `pageerror` count is 0.
Given the XSS payload, when rendered, then `window.__xss` is undefined and `page.locator('img[onerror], script:not([src])')` inside the message area has count 0.
Given a completed signed-in chat, when browser storage is dumped, then the ID token string appears in none of localStorage, sessionStorage or IndexedDB.

questions: Playwright against what: stubbed API plus Firebase Auth emulator (assumed in E8-T10) or the real compose stack with an Identity Platform test tenant? The arch names tests but not the harness.
Firebase web SDK config (apiKey, authDomain) delivery: assumed VITE_* build-time env; arch does not say how the SPA gets it, nor how E10 injects it into the bucket build.
Does GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages return retrieval_degraded and the user's prior feedback score? 6.1 only says 'messages with citations (redacted)'; E8-T8/T9 assume they may be absent.
Arch does not define an escalation action for refusal escalate_offer=true (only GET /v1/escalations exists); E8-T6 shows a hint only.
Client retry limits and backoff for SSE resume are not specified (SSE_* config keys are server-side); E8-T5 uses constants chosen at implementation.
Kong/ALB must pass `Last-Event-ID` and not buffer SSE for the same-origin SPA; assumed handled in E4/E10.
